# @game-studio/event

A package to create custom events. 

This package uses it's own implementation of linked lists with a custom node pooling system to prevent the  dispatching flow from being disrupted when nodes are removed.

## Usage

#### General Usage Example:
```Javascript
// Import event from the package
import { Event1 } from '@game-studio/event';

// Create a new event that will dispatch with 1 arguments a number and a string
const onExampleFoo = new Event1<number>();

// Add a Listener to the event to be invoked when a dispatch has been invoked
onExampleFoo.addListener((num: number) => { 
    console.log(num);
});

// Dispatch this event with an argument of: 321
onExampleFoo.dispatch(321);

```

## Public Getters

`listenerCount` - This is a getter that will return amount of listeners that are on the current event.

#### Example:
```Javascript
onExampleFoo.addListener(() => { 
    // empty arrow function
});

console.log(onExampleFoo.listenerCount); // Console Output:1
```

`isDispatching` - This is a getter that will return if the current event is dispatching.

#### Example:
```Javascript
onExampleFoo.addListener(() => { 
    console.log(onExampleFoo.isDipatching);
});

console.log(onExampleFoo.isDipatching); // Console Output: false
onExampleFoo.dispatch();                // Console Output: true
```

## Public Methods

`addListener` - This accepts a function that has the same or less parameters as the event. This will add a listener to be invoked when the event is dispatched.

#### Example:
```Javascript
onExampleFoo.addListener((num: number) => { 
    console.log(num);
});

onExampleFoo.dispatch(123);             // Console Output: 123
onExampleFoo.dispatch(456);             // Console Output: 456
```

`addListenerOnce` - This accepts a function that has the same or less parameters as the event. This will add a listener to be invoked once when the event is dispatched.

#### Example:
```Javascript
onExampleFoo.addListenerOnce((num: number) => {
    console.log(num);
});

onExampleFoo.dispatch(123);             // Console Output: 123
onExampleFoo.dispatch(456);             // Console Output:
```

`removeListener` - This accepts a function of the listener that you wish to remove. It will only remove the first occurence of the same listener in the linked list from head to tail.

#### Example:
```Javascript
function fooFunc (num: number): void { 
    console.log(num);
}

onExampleFoo.addListener(fooFunc);
onExampleFoo.removeListener(fooFunc);

onExampleFoo.dispatch(123);             // Console Output:
```

`removeAllListeners` - This accepts no parameters and will remove all of the current listeners from an event.

#### Example:
```Javascript
function fooFunc1 (num: number): void { 
    console.log(num);
}

function fooFunc2 (num: number): void { 
    console.log(num);
}

onExampleFoo.addListener(fooFunc1);
onExampleFoo.addListener(fooFunc2);

onExampleFoo.removeAllListeners();

onExampleFoo.dispatch(123);             // Console Output:
```

`dispatch` - This requires the parameters that match the generic types used when instantiating the event. This method will then execute every listener in the linked list with that data.

#### Example:
```Javascript
function fooFunc (num: number): void { 
    console.log(num);
}

onExampleFoo.addListener(fooFunc);

onExampleFoo.dispatch(123);             // Console Output: 123
```

## Development

### How It Works Internally

Listeners are stored inside the main doubly linked list. Everytime an event listener is added a node will be pulled from the node pool and added to the main linked list. If the pool is empty it will construct a blank new node and return that.

When you dispatch the event the arguments will be passed to `state.dispatchEvent` to be invoked on the listeners. The state will change from `NonDispatchingState` to `DispatchingState` so that any changes made to the listeners while dispatching will be temporarily put in a queue rather than changing them instantly and disrupting the dispatch flow. The state change also prevents start and end dispatching from being excuted prematurely when firing an event inside of an event.

Once the event has finished dispatching it will then remove all listeners that were queued to be removed and add all listener queued to be added into the listener linked list. It will also switch back to the `NonDispatchingState` meaning changes to the listener linked list will change immediatly.

#### States

DispatchingState - `DispatchingState` purpose is to queue new nodes or prepare nodes to be removed once the dispatch has finished. It also prevents `startDispatching` and `endDispatching` from being invoked while already dispatching.

NonDispatchingState - The `NonDispatchingState` actualy removes and add's nodes directly to the doubly linked list. It is responsible for switching to and from the `DispatchingState`. When we dispatch an event we switch state to the dispatching state and start executing our listeners. Once we have finished invoking the listeners we will remove and add the nodes that were queue'd to be added or removed.
